BiblicalUsage: The lion is the king of beasts in Scripture, feared and admired in the same breath. Judah is a lion's whelp in Jacob's blessing, David tells Saul he killed a lion that took a lamb, the proverb makes a wicked ruler a roaring lion over the poor, and Amos asks who can but prophesy when the lion has roared.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the lion shows us two things at once: the strength God gives His people, and the strength of the enemies they face. David's lion and Amos's lion are the same animal, and the difference is whose side it is on, which is why I hold that the Lion of Judah is the only lion worth fearing and the only one worth following.
